q: What is the travelling salesperson problem asking for?
options: A minimum-cost cycle that visits every city exactly once
The shortest path between two cities
A cycle using every road exactly once
explain: It is a minimum-cost Hamiltonian cycle. Using every road once would be an Euler circuit.

q: How many different tours start at a fixed city in a TSP with n cities and an asymmetric cost matrix?
explain: The other n − 1 cities can be visited in any order. If the matrix is symmetric, each tour and its reverse cost the same, which halves this.

q: Why is the total subtracted by reducing the cost matrix a lower bound on every tour?
options: Every tour uses exactly one entry from each row and each column
Because the smallest entries form a tour
explain: A tour leaves each city once (one entry per row) and enters each city once (one per column), so it pays at least each row's and each column's minimum.

q: The rows of a 4 × 4 cost matrix have minima 10, 8, 7 and 6. After subtracting them, the column minima are 0, 0, 0 and 1. What is the root bound?
explain: 31 from the rows plus 1 from the columns.

q: To compute the child for edge (i, j), which entries are set to ∞ before reducing?
options: Row i, column j and the entry (j, start)
explain: City i is left only once and city j is entered only once. Blocking (j, start) stops the tour from closing early.

q: What is the bound of the child for edge (i, j)?
options: bound(parent) + A[i][j] + reduction of the child matrix
reduction of the child matrix only
explain: A is the parent's reduced matrix: its entry (i, j) is the extra cost of using that edge above what the bound already counts.

q: Which live node does LC branch and bound expand next in a minimisation problem?
options: The one with the smallest lower bound
The one with the largest bound
explain: Least-cost means the most promising node first. FIFO takes the oldest node.

q: In FIFO branch and bound, the first complete tour found is always optimal.
explain: False. In the page's example FIFO first finds a tour of cost 54 and only later the optimal 38.

q: On the 4-city example on this page, how many nodes do LC and FIFO expand?
explain: LC goes straight down the cheapest branch; FIFO must finish two whole levels first.

q: The reduced-matrix bound works for asymmetric cost matrices as well as symmetric ones.
explain: True. The argument (one entry per row and per column) never uses symmetry.
